items.stem: In C#, what is the most reliable first step when the toolchain reports a syntax error on a line?

options.text: Read the error message and its location, then inspect that line and the one above it
options.rationale: Correct: the message and position point directly at the fault, which often starts on the previous line.

options.text: Rewrite the whole program from scratch
options.rationale: Wasteful and does not teach you what was wrong.

options.text: Ignore the error and run the program again
options.rationale: The error stops the program; running again changes nothing.

options.text: Delete the reported line without reading it
options.rationale: This removes needed logic without understanding the cause.

items.explanation: Correct: the message and position point directly at the fault, which often starts on the previous line.

items.stem: Which TWO statements about variables in C# are correct? (Select TWO.)

options.text: A variable must be assigned a value before it is read
options.rationale: Correct: reading an unassigned variable is a common beginner error.

options.text: A descriptive variable name makes a program easier to read and maintain
options.rationale: Correct: clear names communicate intent to future readers.

options.text: Variable names may freely begin with a digit
options.rationale: Identifiers generally cannot start with a digit.

options.text: Choosing a variable name changes how fast the program runs
options.rationale: Names do not affect runtime behaviour.

items.explanation: Correct: reading an unassigned variable is a common beginner error.

items.stem: A loop that should run ten times instead runs forever. What is the most likely cause?

options.text: The loop's termination condition never becomes false because the counter is not updated
options.rationale: Correct: without progress toward the exit condition the loop never ends.

options.text: The program has too many comments
options.rationale: Comments do not affect control flow.
Speed does not cause an infinite loop.

options.text: Loops are not allowed to run ten times

items.explanation: Correct: without progress toward the exit condition the loop never ends.
